_comment: The protected-path families shared-governance PR 3 adds (docs/CONTRACTS.md §37): what
`secret_path` and `ci_path` protect when [governance] (or a role governance table) is declared
and [governance.paths] does not declare the list. A declared list REPLACES its default; an empty
list protects nothing. With no governance declared neither family exists.
Pattern forms: `name` (no slash) is the last component of a path, anywhere; `dir/x/**` is
relative to the repository root and names the directory too; `~/...` is under the home
directory; `/...` is absolute; `!pattern` excepts. The last matching pattern decides.
`env_dumpers` is the fixed list (shell.ts bashEnvDump, ENV_DUMP_PATH) in the secrets family; no
list declares it away. packages/gnomon-core/src/protected_paths.test.ts pins this file against
env_dumpers: printenv (bare, or naming a variable outside PATH, HOME, USER, LANG, TERM, NODE_ENV, XDG_*, …)

secret_path: bash (a word naming one, a redirection, an env dump, a recursive reader reaching one)
grep / glob (the scope, or a scope above a listed directory)
